column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew emphasizes weighing by repeating its root.
The Hebrew explicitly says now; BSB says then.
The Hebrew says the arrows are with him without explicitly saying they pierced him.

The Hebrew describes his request coming; BSB uses a passive grant.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes his exulting in unrelenting pain; BSB makes joy something the fact brings him.
The Hebrew says his end and pictures patience as prolonging his soul; BSB says future and patient.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew coordinates the absence of help and success being driven away; BSB makes the latter a now that clause.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes flowing or passing streams; BSB explicitly calls them seasonal and says they overflow.
The Hebrew describes snow hidden upon them; BSB supplies melting snow flowing in.
The Hebrew says their place; BSB specifies channels.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the object of looking unnamed and says they hoped for them; BSB supplies water and finding it.
The Hebrew has a singular subject for trusting and plural subjects for arriving and being ashamed.
The Hebrew continues the comparison with the stream; BSB describes them as of no help.
The Hebrew asks for a payment on his behalf; BSB says offer me a bribe.
The Hebrew pictures the ruthless as a hand; BSB says grasp.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the words forceful; BSB says painful. It repeats the root for correction.
The Hebrew calls them a despairing person’s sayings, rather than explicitly my cry.

The Hebrew twice commands returning and says his righteousness is in it; BSB interprets reconsidering and being at stake.
The Hebrew names the palate; BSB says mouth.
